wing-commitment.name: Committed to the Bit
wing-commitment.subtitle: Seeing It Through
wing-commitment.statement: A saint in a foil hat, a magpie matching a parade kick for kick, an artist emptying themselves onto the paper, a wrestler carrying a crate of rubber monsters to its logical conclusion. Nobody here is doing the thing halfway. That's the whole exhibition.

wing-spare-parts.name: Spare Parts
wing-spare-parts.subtitle: Bodies, Assembled Wrongly
wing-spare-parts.statement: Everything here has been put together out of more parts than a body usually needs, or fewer. A shop's worth of blank figures, a winged thing hung up and catalogued, a hydra grown from one cylinder, a man with a third arm wired to his ribs. The dark background is doing them all a favour.

wing-wrong-size.name: The Wrong Size
wing-wrong-size.subtitle: Scale as Punchline
wing-wrong-size.statement: A balloon creature jammed into a hallway, a two-storey eyeball parked on grass, and a party balloon chained to the floor. Each one is a cheerful object that has been given either far too much mass or far too much room. The banal setting is what makes it land.

wing-long-pose.name: The Long Pose
wing-long-pose.subtitle: Skin, Held Still
wing-long-pose.statement: Five bodies arranged by somebody: a lover, an illustrator, a photographer with a very hard flash. Some are drawn in three confident lines and some are lit until they turn into sculpture, but all of them are holding a position for the length of time it takes to make a picture. The strain is part of the subject.

wing-anachronism.name: The Anachronism Department
wing-anachronism.subtitle: Eras, Improperly Mixed
wing-anachronism.statement: A pharaoh with a Kalashnikov, a wrestler and a vocaloid sharing a logo, a tomb wall worn as a collar, a crane whose head has been replaced by pixels. Each of these takes two periods that should never meet and renders both with total conviction. Nobody in here is winking.

wing-plain-evidence.name: Plain Evidence
wing-plain-evidence.subtitle: Objects, Photographed Flatly
wing-plain-evidence.statement: Four photographs that do nothing clever: a hand held up to a marble hand, a Soviet orbit computer opened to show its gears, a road losing an argument with a dune, a rifle alone in an empty flat. The framing is estate-agent neutral in every case. The object is left to carry the entire story, and each one does.

wing-polite-monsters.name: Polite Monsters
wing-polite-monsters.subtitle: Menace, Well Behaved
wing-polite-monsters.statement: A horned man resting his hands on someone's shoulders for the portrait, a black cloud grinning inside a bottle, an elder god sitting in lotus with a smiley mask strapped over its face. All three are alarming and all three are being very good about it. The dark room lets the eyes and teeth do the work.

wing-signal-loss.name: Signal Loss
wing-signal-loss.subtitle: Images, Coming Apart
wing-signal-loss.statement: Three pictures that were perfectly fine until part of them stopped rendering. A train smeared into horizontal stripes, a fashion portrait with one rectangle slid out of place, a woman downsampled panel by panel until she's a sprite. In each case the undamaged part stays calm, which is the only reason the damage reads as a decision.

wing-escalation.name: The Escalation Room
wing-escalation.subtitle: Loops That Worsen
wing-escalation.statement: Three clips that begin merely odd and then commit: a tree disappearing into a wall of giraffe necks, a chrome skeleton walking a fighter into the fence, a cartoon face compressing itself out of existence one caption at a time. None of them resolves; each just gets more of whatever it already was. Benches provided, because they are all on a loop.

wing-devotional-diagrams.name: Devotional Diagrams
wing-devotional-diagrams.subtitle: Reverence, Technically Drawn
wing-devotional-diagrams.statement: Three pictures wearing the clothes of holy images: a votive candle print watched by an enormous eye, a rose window assembled from bullet holes, an annunciation woodcut annotated with codes that key to nothing. Each borrows a layout designed for awe and fills it with statistics, labels or static. The gilt frames are not a joke at their expense; they are what the pictures were already asking for.

wing-too-many-hands.name: The Wrong Number of Hands
wing-too-many-hands.subtitle: Reaching, Uninvited
wing-too-many-hands.statement: Three paintings of a girl who has more arms than the situation requires, and one old book illustration where a single extra hand is more than enough. In the paintings the surplus is calm, decorative, almost bored; in the illustration it has hold of an ankle. Between them sits the whole question of whether a hand arriving from nowhere is a blessing or a grab.

wing-fine-grain.name: The Fine Grain
wing-fine-grain.subtitle: Detail Past Reading
wing-fine-grain.statement: Four images that keep subdividing until the eye hands in its notice: a 1963 drawing halving its own squares into grey, an 1869 plate of capillaries branching into mesh, a field of gold circuit boards tiled to the horizon, and a corrupted board humming in place. Each starts legible on one side and ends as texture on the other. Stand close and then stand back; they are different pictures from each distance.

wing-somewhere-to-stand.name: Somewhere to Stand
wing-somewhere-to-stand.subtitle: Invented Architecture
wing-somewhere-to-stand.statement: A shopping atrium with stars in the ceiling, a hatched city seen from the pipework below it, and a pixel station platform with a planet parked outside. All three are interiors built for someone, and in each the population has been reduced to one figure or none. The lights are on, the escalators are running, and nobody is coming.

wing-wet-hardware.name: Wet Hardware
wing-wet-hardware.subtitle: Flesh, Plugged In
wing-wet-hardware.statement: A tower PC growing organs around a fish head, a column of CRTs bagged in offal and still being typed into, and a slab of bone-in meat that would like you to know it is a god. The flesh in these pictures isn't presented as a wound; it's a component, installed, seated correctly, apparently working. The room is dark so that you have to walk up close to see what's in the bags.

wing-understudies.name: The Understudies
wing-understudies.subtitle: Cast As Something Else
wing-understudies.statement: Two puppies and a crayfish accidentally restaging the Moon card, sheep knitted out of telephone cable, a microSD laid on a tongue like a wafer, and two dolls filming a fifteen-second friendship with a title card at the end. Each picture has cast something in a role it was never built for, and in each case the casting holds. None of them is trying very hard to convince you, which is exactly why it works.

wing-everything-at-once.name: Everything At Once
wing-everything-at-once.subtitle: Screens, Fully Loaded
wing-everything-at-once.statement: Five pictures that refuse to leave any space empty: two maximalist paintings with a taskbar running along the bottom edge, a tapestry of the early internet, a teaching diagram that covers an entire curriculum in one image, and a game world that has ground itself into icons and noise. All of them are organised, in the sense that somebody very clearly had a system. Working out what it was is the visitor's problem.
